terms.definition: Recreational searching for and collecting minerals, including gold. In Australian usage it can also include gems; New Zealand uses ‘gold fossicking’ for recreational gold recovery. The word itself does not grant access or permission.
terms.locator: NSW Introduction; DOC Introduction and rules

terms.definition: A metal vessel for breaking small ore samples with a heavy hand-held rod called a dolly. Think of a rugged mortar and pestle for rock sampling.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.96 / PDF p.102: dolly; dolly pot

terms.definition: The heavy metal hand tool used to pound ore inside a dolly pot. In this glossary’s Australian source, it names the pounding tool rather than the pot.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.96 / PDF p.102: dolly

terms.definition: Another name for a gold pan: a shallow, sloping-sided dish used to wash sediment and retain heavy particles.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.97 / PDF p.103: pan; prospector’s dish

terms.definition: Goldfields slang for a claim, shaft or mine that proves unproductive or unprofitable.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.96 / PDF p.102: duffer

terms.definition: An old gold-bearing watercourse buried beneath later sediment or rock. Here ‘lead’ means a line of deposit, not the metal.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.96 / PDF p.102: Deep Lead

terms.definition: Waste rock removed during mining, often piled in a mullock heap. It is distinct from the finer material left after ore processing, commonly called tailings.
terms.locator: Waste rock; Mining sand

terms.definition: The framework above a mine shaft that holds the pulleys for hoisting ropes; also called a headframe.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.97 / PDF p.103: headframe; poppet head

terms.definition: A double-faced hammer used to strike a hand steel or drill in rock work; the Gympie history describes examples weighing four to six pounds.
terms.locator: Glossary, printed p.97 / PDF p.103: Gympie hammer

terms.definition: Searching by eye for loose gold exposed on the ground, then picking it up from the surface. Historical accounts distinguish this from digging or washing sediment.
terms.locator: Siberia detrital deposits discussion: prospecting known as ‘specking’

terms.definition: In gold-rush accounts, a person working the diggings for gold—a miner or prospector. The word has other meanings outside this setting.
terms.locator: Gold diggers; mining methods and toolkit

terms.definition: A rocking gold-washing box, also called a rocker box. Water and a rocking motion help lighter sediment wash away while gold collects inside.
terms.locator: Shovel, pan and cradle; Victorian diggers’ toolkit

terms.definition: A name for long, stepped wooden gold-washing boxes. Riffles retain heavy material as water carries lighter sediment onward. The nickname is not exclusive to New Zealand.
terms.locator: Sluice boxes

terms.definition: A constructed channel bringing water from a creek to mining workings. A surviving race is a historical feature, not an indication that prospecting is allowed there.
terms.locator: Sluice boxes: channels bringing water to workings

terms.definition: A nozzle that directs a powerful jet of water at gold-bearing gravel during hydraulic mining. This is industrial mining equipment, not a small panning accessory.
terms.locator: Sluicing

terms.definition: A mineralized vein followed by hard-rock miners; gold-bearing quartz veins are often called reefs in New Zealand mining histories. It does not mean a coral reef.
terms.locator: Hard-rock mining

terms.definition: A set of crushing stamps that breaks quartz ore before gold recovery. ‘Battery’ means a group of machines, not an electrical power source.
terms.locator: Hard-rock mining

terms.definition: A hand-operated suction tube best known for collecting fishing bait. Some prospectors use or adapt these pumps to gather submerged sediment for panning; this equipment description does not establish where pumping is permitted.
terms.locator: Product description; stated river/stream gold-prospecting use

terms.definition: A nickname for a suction device used to collect sediment from bedrock cracks. A New Zealand prospecting discussion also calls it a crevice sucker or gravel pump; the names are used elsewhere too.
terms.locator: Gavin’s opening post, 22 February 2010; equipment-name usage only

terms.definition: A newcomer to the North. Gold-rush accounts contrast an inexperienced cheechako with a seasoned sourdough; the term describes regional experience, not nationality.
terms.locator: Cheechako Hill opening; NPS report PDF p.243, old-timer/new-arrival distinction

terms.definition: An experienced northern old-timer, often a veteran of prospecting life in Yukon or Alaska. In this usage it describes a person, rather than bread or a starter.
terms.locator: Cheechako Hill opening; NPS report PDF p.243, old-timer/new-arrival distinction

terms.definition: A gold-washing pan or bowl, traditionally made of wood or metal and often conical. Colombian mining terminology uses it for concentrating heavy minerals from sediment or crushed samples.
terms.locator: Batea entry; PDF p.9

terms.definition: Washing sediment in a batea to separate heavy minerals, including gold. The activity name does not by itself establish permission to collect.
terms.locator: Bateo entry, PDF p.9; Martín abstract on gold panning in Granada

terms.definition: Manual washing of sand to recover precious metals, without machinery or mechanical assistance, in the Colombian mining glossary. Mazamorreo is another recorded name. This definition is not a summary of current permit rules.
terms.locator: Barequeo and Bateo entries; PDF p.9

terms.definition: A gold-washing pan or dish used to concentrate heavy minerals by density. BRGM distinguishes the batée from a grooved Californian pan and a Finnish-style flat pan.
terms.locator: Section 5, printed p.46 / PDF p.50; Figure 34

terms.definition: A small, rounded metal bowl used for the final separation of small quantities of gold concentrate, as described in BRGM’s French Guiana study.
terms.locator: Section 5, Le Couy; printed p.47 / PDF p.51; Figure 36

terms.definition: A person who washes river sediment to recover gold; more broadly, a gold seeker. Orpailleuse is a recorded feminine form. It is an occupational word, not inherently a joke or slang.
terms.locator: Orpailleur definition and feminine-form note

terms.definition: Gold recovery or working by an orpailleur, especially from alluvial deposits. French Guiana sources use it for mining activity, so it should not automatically be translated as casual hobby panning.
terms.locator: BRGM alluvial-gold production and provenance discussion; Académie occupational definition

terms.definition: A bowl for washing gold-bearing sediment, often with a conical base. Brazilian museum examples include wooden pans; metal and plastic versions are also used.
terms.locator: Museum object description; glossary Batéia and Bateiar, printed p.117 / PDF p.118

terms.definition: Artisanal mineral workings or the activity of working them, often associated with gold and gems. It can involve alluvial or primary deposits; the word does not mean that every operation is recreational or legal.
terms.locator: Garimpo entry, printed pp.119–120 / PDF pp.120–121

terms.definition: A person working in a garimpo, commonly an artisanal miner seeking gold or gems. Garimpeira is the feminine form.
terms.locator: Museum discussion of women working in garimpos; glossary’s Bamburrado and Garimpo entries

terms.definition: A lucky rich strike that brings sudden wealth in a garimpo. The related word bamburrado describes a miner who has struck it rich.
terms.locator: Bamburro and Bamburrado entries; printed p.117 / PDF p.118

terms.definition: A small wooden sluice used to wash gravel in manual garimpo workings, recorded in Brazil’s mining glossary. It names equipment, not an animal encountered while prospecting.
terms.locator: Cobra-fumando entry; printed p.118 / PDF p.119

terms.definition: A name used by a German prospecting-equipment maker for a piston hand pump that sucks sediment from bedrock cracks. Its listing also uses the English nickname ‘Gold Sucker’.
terms.locator: Product title and description: piston, suction and bedrock crevices

terms.definition: A German term for a gold pan. Equipment listings use it alongside the English ‘Gold Pan’; it is a translated tool name rather than a separate recovery method.
terms.locator: Related product: Goldwaschpfanne SE Gold Pan
